Article Title: Can Kimi Antonelli clinch the F1 2026 title in Austin? How does the championship race stand with Russell, Hamilton and Verstappen still in contention?
Article Text:
Kimi Antonelli is leading the drivers' standings in F1. (Image credit: F1/Instagram)

Kimi Antonelli (Getty Images)

Current points: 340 | Championship lead: 102 points

2. George Russell: The closest challenger

Mercedes driver George Russell

Current points: 238 | Gap to Antonelli: 102 points

3. Lewis Hamilton: Ferrari needs a huge turnaround

Lewis Hamilton (Image credit: Getty Images)

Current points: 229 | Gap to Antonelli: 111 points

4. Max Verstappen: The Singapore winner needs another charge

Red Bull's Max Verstappen (Reuters)

Current points: 221 | Gap to Antonelli: 119 points

Leclerc and Norris face an uphill battle

Can Antonelli seal the title in Austin?

Max Verstappen has mounted another second-half comeback, much like in 2025. In his last 10 races, he has suffered two DNFs, won back-to-back races in Malaysia and Singapore, and collected six podiums. But despite his recent form, the championship remains a long way out of his reach as Kimi Antonelli closes in on the title.Formula 1 has reached the stage of the season where the title fight is no longer just about race results. The points table is beginning to tell its own story, and Antonelli has a sizeable advantage over the chasing pack.The Mercedes youngster finished third at the Singapore Grand Prix, where Verstappen took victory. George Russell could manage only ninth after starting from the back because of an engine penalty, allowing Antonelli to extend his championship lead to 102 points.Antonelli now has 340 points, Russell is on 238, Lewis Hamilton has 229, Verstappen sits on 221, Charles Leclerc has 215, and Lando Norris is on 201. Six races remain, with a maximum of 150 points still available. All six are mathematically in contention, but the task facing Antonelli's rivals is becoming increasingly difficult.The next stop is Austin, Texas, from October 23 to 25. Antonelli has an opportunity to become the youngest Formula 1 world champion in history, although the title cannot be decided by his result alone. The other contenders' finishes will also determine whether the championship remains open.If Antonelli wins in Austin, he will move to 365 points. For the title to be decided that weekend, Russell must finish ninth or lower, while Hamilton must finish fifth or lower. Verstappen's result will also be crucial.If Russell finishes ninth, he will move to 240 points, leaving him 125 behind Antonelli with only 125 points available after Austin. Antonelli would retain the advantage on countback because he has already won more races.If Hamilton finishes fifth, he will reach 239 points, putting him 126 behind Antonelli and beyond reach with five rounds remaining.Antonelli's Mercedes teammate Russell remains his closest challenger, but the gap has now stretched to more than four race wins. He has 238 points and can collect a maximum of 150 more across the final six Grands Prix.If Russell wins every remaining race, he would finish on 388 points. Even then, the title would not be guaranteed. Antonelli would need to score no more than 47 points across those six races for Russell to finish ahead.Seven-time world champion Lewis Hamilton has 229 points, 111 behind Antonelli. He can reach a maximum of 379 points if he wins all six remaining Grands Prix.For Hamilton to finish ahead, Antonelli would need to score no more than 38 points over the same period. Austin is particularly important. If Antonelli wins, Hamilton must finish fourth or better to keep his title hopes mathematically alive. A fifth-place finish or lower would leave him too far behind with five races remaining.Verstappen will arrive in Austin after back-to-back victories in Malaysia and Singapore. The Red Bull driver has shown he can put together a late-season winning run, but he remains 119 points behind Antonelli despite his recent results.Verstappen can reach 371 points if he wins every remaining Grand Prix. To finish ahead of Antonelli, he needs to gain at least 120 points on the championship leader over the final six rounds. Even if Verstappen wins all six, Antonelli can score no more than 30 points during that period for the Red Bull driver to finish ahead.Charles Leclerc and Lando Norris also face a steep climb. Leclerc has 215 points, while Norris is sixth with 201. Leclerc can reach 365 points by winning every remaining race, while Norris can finish on a maximum of 351. Both need a major swing in results, with Antonelli dropping points while they produce near-perfect finishes.If Antonelli wins in Austin, Leclerc and Norris will be eliminated from championship contention, provided the other results leave the Italian beyond their reach.Antonelli's 102-point lead gives him a strong chance of wrapping up the championship early, but the outcome in Austin depends on the results of his closest rivals.He needs to win, Russell must finish ninth or lower, and Hamilton must finish fifth or lower. Verstappen must also fail to win for Antonelli to clinch the title that weekend.If those results fall into place, Antonelli will become the youngest world champion in Formula 1 history. Otherwise, the championship fight will continue into the remaining five rounds.
Article Summary: Kimi Antonelli extends his championship lead to 102 points. The Ferrari driver is one win away from becoming the youngest F1 world champion. Lewis Hamilton, Max Verstappen, Charles Leclerc and Lando Norris are also in contention.

Article Title: India's para track and field stars lead golden surge at Asian Para Games
Article Text:
Dilip Mahadu Gavit (IANS)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

India’s para-athletes continued to swell the medal tally with a superb haul of gold medals on Thursday, as Shailesh Kumar spearheaded a podium sweep in the men’s high jump T63, Anjanaben Bumbadiya triumphed in the women’s 400m T47, and Dilip Mahadu Gavit secured his second gold of the Games in Nagoya.Defending champion Dharmaraj Solairaj smashed the Asian record in the men’s T44/T62/T64 long jump, while Suvarna Raj clinched gold in the women’s F54 discus throw, underlining the nation’s growing strength across para-athletics disciplines.Shailesh produced a Games-record leap of 1.89m to take the high jump gold. Former Paralympic bronze medallist Varun Bhati claimed silver with a season’s best of 1.84m, while Rahul completed the Indian clean sweep with 1.81m.Bumbadiya clocked 59.97s to win the women’s 400m T47 title, with compatriot Jayanti Behera taking silver in 1:00.65. Thailand’s Sasirawan Inthachot finished third in 1:02.58.Gavit, who had won the men’s 100m T47 gold on Wednesday, added another yellow metal by winning the 400m in 48.27s. Bhavikkumar Bharwad initially finished second in 49.31s but was disqualified for a second lane infringement. Japan’s Kakeru Ishida was consequently upgraded to silver, while Uzbekistan’s Marufjon Murodulloev took bronze.Solairaj, a 32-year-old Tamil Nadu jumper, registered 7.15m in his second attempt to break the Asian record. Malaysia’s Eddy Bernard won silver with 6.34m, while Japan’s Yuma Tamaki secured bronze with 6.89m.Suvarna, 44, delivered a winning discus throw of 15.66m. Iran’s Shahla Hadidi took silver with 15.45m and Vietnam’s Thi Ngoc Thuy Nguyen won bronze with 14.65m. India added further podium finishes through visually impaired Tejalben Damor, who won silver in the women’s 400m T12 in 57.60 seconds after her 200m bronze, and Ravanni Valasanaini, who claimed bronze in the women’s 400m T11 with a personal best of 1:03.64.India has so far won 52 medals from para-athletics, with 18 gold, 16 silver and 18 bronze after the end of Day 4 of the competitions.
Article Summary: Shailesh Kumar leads podium sweep in men's high jump T63. Anjanaben Bumbadiya wins women's 400m T47 title. Dilip Mahadu Gavit secures his second gold of the Games in Nagoya.

Article Title: Asian Para Games: Sandeep, Haney strike gold with world-record feats as India hit 100 medals
Article Text:
Sandeep sets T44 world record (Image: ANI)

Sandeep sets world record, Ajay Kumar claims bronze

Haney breaks world record with 60.49m javelin throw

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

India reach 100-medal milestone

India's golden run at the Aichi-Nagoya 2026 Asian Para Games gathered further momentum on Friday as Sandeep and Haney clinched gold medals with world-record performances in their respective events, taking the country's overall medal tally to 100. Sandeep set a new world record in the men's 400m T64, while Haney produced a record-breaking throw in the men's javelin F37/38 final at the Nagoya City Mizuho Park Athletic Stadium.Sandeep clocked 52.28 seconds to win the men's 400m final, finishing comfortably ahead of Saudi Arabia's Nour Alsana, who secured silver in 53.13 seconds, a season's best. India's Ajay Kumar claimed bronze in 53.61 seconds, setting a Games record, while China's Huang Ruihua finished fourth with a personal-best time of 54.39 seconds.In the men's 400m, athletes from the T44 and T64 classifications competed together. While Sandeep and Alsana belong to the T44 category, Ajay Kumar competes in T64. Both classifications cover athletes with lower-limb impairments.Haney followed with a world-record throw of 60.49 metres to claim gold in the men's javelin F37/38 event, earning 1,116 Raza points. Iran's Hormoz Seidikazpounji took silver with a personal-best throw of 50.68 metres, earning 1,009 points, while China's Yu Chengjie secured bronze with an Asian-record effort of 53.66 metres and 943 points.The combined F37 and F38 javelin categories are decided using Raza points, which account for the different classifications. This explains why Seidikazpounji finished ahead of Yu despite recording a shorter throw.The double world-record triumph marked another significant milestone for India, whose overall medal tally crossed 100 at the Aichi-Nagoya 2026 Asian Para Games.
Article Summary: India reach 100-medal milestone at the Aichi-Nagoya 2026 Asian Para Games. Sandeep and Haney clinch gold medals with world-record performances in their respective events, taking the country's overall medal tally to 100. Haney breaks world record with 60.49m javelin throw.

Article Title: India tour of New Zealand: Red-hot Shikhar Mohan earns India A call-up; set to replace KL Rahul for two fixtures
Article Text:
Shikhar Mohan (PTI Photo)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Jharkhand opener Shikhar Mohan has received a maiden India A call-up for the last two four-day matches against New Zealand. The 21-year-old will replace KL Rahul, who will join the ODI squad after playing the first four-day match against New Zealand A, starting on Saturday at Bert Sutcliffe Oval at Lincoln University.The southpaw has continued his red-hot form with back-to-back hundreds in the ongoing Ranji Trophy season. Shikhar smashed 143 against Kerala in Jamshedpur and then scored a match-saving 127 against Maharashtra in Pune.Shikhar's mentor, Ishank Jaggi, a former Jharkhand cricketer, has heaped praise on the youngster, saying the time is absolutely ripe for him to take the next step."It is perfect timing. He is in good form. Scored two centuries in Ranji. Had a great Duleep Trophy final and Irani Trophy as well," Jaggi told TimesofIndia.com.After an excellent debut season in 2025-26, in which he amassed 613 runs at an average of 55.73, including two centuries, he has started the new season in rollicking fashion, smashing 143 in Jharkhand's opening match against Kerala at the Keenan Stadium in Jamshedpur.The southpaw also made some valuable contributions in the Duleep Trophy final for East Zone, scoring 85 and 52 in the two innings, followed by a solid 60 on a green top in Srinagar in the Irani Trophy, playing for Rest of India against defending Ranji Trophy champions Jammu and Kashmir.Jaggi, who is currently coaching the Jharkhand U-23 side, says Shikhar Mohan has been in top form for the past four to five years."Look, he has been in good form for the last four to five years. He has dominated age-group cricket as well. I feel this is a great time for him to have this experience. It will be great exposure for him. He will realise what he needs to add to his game and will come back as a better cricketer," says Jaggi, who has played 90 First Class matches.Jaggi is correct about the southpaw's rich vein of form. Shikhar Mohan enjoyed significant success with the Under-23 side in the Col CK Nayudu Trophy. In the 2023-24 season, he scored 623 runs, including two hundreds and three fifties. He continued his run-scoring spree the following season, scoring 887 runs, which helped him earn a call-up to the senior side.One issue with Shikhar's batting, which the youngster himself has admitted to, is his inability to convert starts into big scores, something he is working on with Jaggi."In my first year of Under-19 cricket, I scored around 550 runs, with most of my scores in the 70s and 80s. The following year, I wanted to focus more and convert those starts into bigger scores," he had told this website."Before facing a ball, I talk to myself. I remind myself to watch the ball and stay focused. That has helped me a lot. Jaggi bhai also helped me with this, especially when he was with the Under-19 team. I started concentrating more and focusing on one ball at a time.That approach has really helped me," he added.Ishank, however, feels the mental block is something even the game's greats have faced."Everyone has gone through that phase. But you have to understand that he is scoring those 70s and 80s consistently, which is no small achievement. He is still raw and can be groomed, and that's why I said this call has come at the right time," he said.Shikhar will travel to New Zealand on October 26 and will link up with the India A squad in Christchurch, where the second four-day game will be played from October 31.
Article Summary: Jharkhand opener Shikhar Mohan has received a maiden India A call-up for the last two four-day matches against New Zealand. The 21-year-old will replace KL Rahul, who will join the ODI squad. The southpaw has continued his red-hot form with back-to-back hundreds in the ongoing Ranji Trophy season.

Article Title: Asian Para Games: India win gold, silver as Anjanaben Bumbadiya, Jayanti Behera ace women's 400m T47 event
Article Text:
Anjanaben Bumbadiya (File Photo)

Sheetal Devi wins two gold medals

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Swati Chaudhary creates history with silver

India enjoyed a successful day at the Asian Para Games on Thursday, with Anjanaben Bumbadiya winning gold and Jayanti Behera taking silver in the women’s 400m T47 event.Anjanaben clocked 59.97 seconds to finish first, becoming the only athlete in the four-runner race to break the one-minute mark.Jayanti finished second in 1:00.65, while Thailand’s Sasirawan Inthachot claimed bronze in 1:02.58.Tejalben Damor also added to India’s medal tally, winning silver in the women’s 400m T12 event with a time of 57.60 seconds.It was her second medal of the Games after taking bronze in the 200m T12 race.Armless archer Sheetal Devi enjoyed another memorable outing, winning gold in both the women’s individual compound and mixed team events. She teamed up with Toman Kumar to beat Indonesia 151-148 in the mixed team final, giving India its first archery gold medal at the Games.Later, Sheetal returned to the range for the individual final against Singapore’s Alim Nur Syahidah. Despite trailing by four points early on, the reigning world champion fought back with accurate shots to win 142-139. The victory marked her second consecutive individual gold at the Asian Para Games.Sheetal, who uses her feet and legs to position the bow and her shoulder and jaw to draw and release the string, finished the day with three medals, including a silver in the women’s compound team event won on Wednesday.However, Toman missed out on an individual medal after losing the men’s bronze playoff to China’s Zhang Yicheng 139-148.Swati Chaudhary became India’s first-ever medallist in the W1 archery category after winning silver in the women’s individual event. She lost 4-6 to China’s Cen Mengkan despite taking a 4-2 lead in the final.Swati won the opening set and regained the lead in the third, but Cen fought back strongly to take the fourth set and force a decider. The Chinese archer then won the final set to secure gold.India now have four medals from archery at the Games, with more opportunities ahead as the men’s and women’s teams remain in contention for gold.
Article Summary: Anjanaben Bumbadiya wins gold in women’s 400m T47 event. Jayanti Behera takes silver in women's 400m event. Sheetal Devi wins two gold medals in archery. Swati Chaudhary becomes India's first-ever medallist in W1 archery category.

Article Title: First time in history! India bowlers make unwanted record as New Zealand run riot
Article Text:
Glenn Phillips runs past Nitish Kumar Reddy during the T20 cricket international between New Zealand and India in Christchurch, New Zealand.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

For the first time in men’s T20I cricket, five Indian bowlers conceded 40 or more runs in an innings as New Zealand piled up 225/8 in the first T20I in Christchurch on Thursday. The hosts took advantage of India's struggles with the ball, with Finn Allen scoring 45 off 24 balls and Glenn Phillips remaining unbeaten on 82 off 40.The feat had occurred 13 times overall in men’s T20Is, but this was the first instance involving five Indian bowlers in the same innings. Bhuvneshwar Kumar conceded 49 runs in four overs, Arshdeep Singh gave away 45, Mayank Yadav 40, Axar Patel 51 and Nitish Reddy 40.New Zealand's total was the joint-highest against India in T20Is and their highest on home soil.With Jasprit Bumrah not part of the squad, the Indian attack struggled to contain the hosts despite some early swing on offer. New Zealand's openers dealt with the movement before taking on the bowlers, with Tim Seifert scoring 24 off 17 balls.Bhuvneshwar, playing his first international match in nearly four years, began with a decent first over. However, Seifert hit him for two fours and a six over long-on in his next over, which cost India 17 runs.Allen then attacked Arshdeep in the following over, which also went for 17 runs, giving New Zealand momentum in the powerplay.The openers were particularly effective at finding boundaries on the off-side.Mayank was brought into the attack during the powerplay and gave India a breakthrough when Seifert was caught behind off the final ball of the fifth over.Axar was handed the final over of the powerplay, but the left-arm spinner conceded two sixes. Allen cleared long-off before Daryl Mitchell stepped out and sent the ball over the long-on boundary. New Zealand reached 65/1 in the first six overs.Arshdeep dismissed Mitchell in his second spell, but Bhuvneshwar continued to struggle. His third over cost 14 runs before he was given the responsibility of bowling the final over, which also went for 14. He finished with figures of 0/49 in four overs.Phillips remained unbeaten and finished the innings with a switch hit over cover. Bevon Jacobs also made an impact with 31 off 16 balls, including a first-ball six down the ground off Arshdeep.New Zealand scored 67 runs in the final five overs to cross the 200-run mark, putting India's bowling attack under pressure throughout the innings.
Article Summary: Bhuvneshwar Kumar, Arshdeep Singh, Mayank Yadav, Axar Patel and Nitish Reddy all gave away 40 or more runs in the same innings. The feat had occurred 13 times overall in men’s T20Is, but this was the first instance involving five Indian bowlers. New Zealand's total was the joint-highest against India in T 20Is and their highest on home soil.

Article Title: No sponsor, a career-threatening setback and one big dream: Nayanika Sanga’s story
Article Text:
Nayanika Sanga (Insta)

NEW DELHI:

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

For Nayanika Sanga, golf has always been about more than the scorecard. As the 22-year-old from Gurugram prepares to compete at the Women’s Indian Open from Oct 22-25 at the DLF Golf and Country Club in Gurugram, she is drawing on lessons learnt over years of competition, international exposure and a difficult comeback from injury. Her approach is simple: concentrate on what she can control, appreciate the opportunity to play and treat every round as a fresh challenge.The philosophy reflects a maturity that has developed through experience. Having travelled abroad for tournaments, including competing in France, Nayanika has learnt to approach the demands of professional golf with greater perspective.“When you play in India, it is like a family. You feel at home and at ease. But when you play outside, the environment is different. People are new, and there can be a language barrier. I think that has made me a little more resilient. When I compete back home now, I feel comfortable because I know the place and the people,” she said.Her journey began when she was five. Her father, who serves in the Navy, wanted her to take up a sport, believing it would help her develop as an individual. She tried squash, tennis and golf, but the response to her natural ability with a club encouraged the family to pursue the latter.Competition soon followed, and the game became a defining part of her life.One of the earliest milestones arrived when she was 11, winning the Kazi Cup at Willingdon Club in Mumbai.“That was definitely a life-changing experience because that was my first win as a child, a big win as a child. Once you start winning, it reinforces that feeling that you want to keep chasing it again and again,” she said.The road since then, however, has not been without setbacks. A wrist injury four years ago came at a particularly difficult time, when she had just turned professional and was playing well. Gratitude journalling became an important part of that process.“When I started playing again, I began focusing on smaller things and feeling grateful that at least today I can play, and tomorrow I can compete. Instead of thinking, ‘I need to win today’, being grateful for the small things in life has definitely helped me,” she said.Physical conditioning has also played a significant role in her return. A professional golfer’s workload extends beyond the hours spent practising and playing. Frequent travel, tournaments scheduled close together and the physical demands of carrying her own bag at overseas events can take a toll. Nayanika credits her strength and conditioning coach, Shaurya Sinha, with helping her rebuild confidence in her body and handle the demands of the circuit.“Because of fitness, I have been a little more resilient to injuries. Other than the injury I had four years ago, I have not had any issues, and I feel my fitness routine is what gets me going every week,” she said.The Women’s Indian Open will present another test. Nayanika regards the DLF Golf and Country Club course as challenging, but prefers to see its demands as an opportunity rather than an obstacle.“I think it is challenging in a fun way. I do not see the course as challenging; rather, every day will be a new challenge there. It will be fun to tackle a new challenge every day,” she said.That outlook also shapes how she approaches a field featuring accomplished players. Rather than becoming preoccupied with the reputations of her opponents, she wants to learn from them while remaining focused on her own performance. She relies more on feel and instinct than data when making decisions on the course, trusting her judgement when she believes her game is in good shape.Nayanika has also witnessed the growth of women’s golf in India. When she first turned professional, she recalled fields of around 30 to 35 players. This year, she said, the numbers have risen to approximately 60 to 62, reflecting greater interest among younger golfers in pursuing the professional route. Lower scores and more opportunities to compete overseas have contributed to the improving standard.Yet the growth of the game has not removed one of its persistent challenges: funding. Despite competing abroad and continuing to develop as a professional, she is still looking for a sponsor. Coming from a middle-class family, with her father serving in the Navy, she knows the financial demands of sustaining a career on tour.“It has been tough. My parents have sacrificed so much for me, and they continue to do so to support me,” she said.Her grandparents also travelled with her to tournaments when she was younger, stepping in whenever her father’s work commitments prevented him from accompanying her. Nayanika acknowledges their contribution.Away from golf, time with friends and playing badminton help her switch off from the constant demands of professional competition. She also looks up to Diksha Dagar and Aditi Ashok whose achievements have out Indian golf on the global map.Nayanika hopes her journey can encourage more young girls to pursue sport, particularly in a society where conventional career choices often dominate expectations.“If you fall in love with a sport, there is nothing better than that feeling. Parents should be willing to explore sporting opportunities when their children show interest and ability,” she said.As she heads into the Women’s Indian Open, her ambitions remain tied to the fundamentals she has learnt through experience: trust her instincts, stay patient and focus on the next shot. For a golfer who has learnt to find perspective in adversity, the challenge is not simply to compete against a strong field, but to keep moving forward, one round at a time.
Article Summary: Nayanika Sanga, 22, will compete at the Women’s Indian Open from Oct 22-25 at the DLF Golf and Country Club in Gurugram. Her approach is simple: concentrate on what she can control, appreciate the opportunity to play and treat every round as a fresh challenge.

Article Title: Three Jharkhand players in India squad for historic lawn bowls series against New Zealand
Article Text:
(From left) Sunil Bahadur, Dinesh Kumar and Reshma Kumari

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Kolkata: Three players from Jharkhand will be part of India’s four-member lawn bowls squad for a historic three-Test series against New Zealand in Nov, part of the centenary celebrations of sporting ties between the two countries.Lawn bowls is one of the only four sports, alongside cricket, hockey and football, selected for the centenary programme.2022 Commonwealth Games silver medallists Dinesh Kumar and Sunil Bahadur and rising player Reshma Kumari, all from Jharkhand, have been selected alongside Arjuna Awardee and Commonwealth Games gold medallist Pinki Singh for the series, scheduled from Nov 16-18 in Auckland.“This is a very important event for us because only four sports are taking part in the centenary celebrations. On the days we are playing, no other sport will be taking place, which means we will receive exclusive coverage,” Bowling Federation of India president Ravi Bengani told TOI in an exclusive interview on Thursday.India will play three Test matches over three days, with each Test comprising five matches — men’s pairs, women’s pairs, mixed fours, mixed pairs 1 and mixed pairs 2.The New Zealand series is part of a broader international exposure programme the federation has put in place as it begins preparations for the 2030 Commonwealth Games in Ahmedabad.A 12-member Indian contingent will travel to Malaysia later this month for a World Bowls-sanctioned tournament, while another group will compete in an invitational event in Hong Kong, where Indian players won bronze medals last year.The federation’s confidence has also received a boost from Putul Sonowal’s recent podium finish at the Champion of Champions event, a first for an Indian player at the prestigious competition.“We have decided to participate in as many World Bowls-sanctioned events as possible. International exposure is crucial if we want to bridge the gap with the leading nations,” Bengani said.The federation is also planning to strengthen its support structure through its partnership with Bowls New Zealand. Bengani revealed that India currently does not have a dedicated national coach, making the proposed knowledge-sharing programme particularly significant.“We have signed an agreement with Bowls New Zealand and now we will have more exchange programmes. We will bring their coaches and technical officials to India and provide our players with greater exposure and expertise,” Bengani said.The plans have gained momentum following the federation’s recognition by the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports earlier this year, a move expected to improve funding and access to high-performance support.As far as the 2030 Commonwealth Games are concerned, the federation has set ambitious targets. “I’m committing to at least four gold medals for India in 2030. Personally, I feel we can win even more if we continue on the current path,” Bengani said.With a packed international calendar, plans to bring in New Zealand coaches and technical experts, and Ahmedabad 2030 on the horizon, the federation believes Indian lawn bowls is entering its most ambitious phase yet.
Article Summary: Lawn bowls is one of the only four sports, alongside cricket, hockey and football, selected for the centenary programme. India will play three Test matches over three days, with each Test comprising five matches. The series is part of a broader international exposure programme the federation has put in place as it begins preparations for the 2030 Commonwealth Games in Ahmedabad.

Article Title: EFI mess costs Indian riders global stage, FEI ban from Dec 1
Article Text:
Equestrian Federation of India

New Delhi:

Yet another tale of administrative chaos and athletes paying the price. Caught in a prolonged governance crisis at the Equestrian Federation of India (EFI), Indian riders now face a ban from international competitions, with their sporting futures hanging in the balance. The latest setback comes at a time when the govt is pushing to bring more international events to India and widen Indian athletes’ exposure to global competition.The International Equestrian Federation (FEI) has decided to suspend the EFI from Dec 1 over prolonged governance irregularities and failure to hold fresh elections, effectively shutting Indian riders, officials, trainers and horses out of international events. TOI is in possession of FEI’s Oct 15 letter confirming the decision, which was taken at the international body's board meeting on Oct 13.Explaining its move, the FEI said the EFI’s prolonged governance crisis had reached a tipping point. “The absence of elections to date to elect a new Executive Committee, has resulted in a prolonged governance and leadership irregularity that is no longer sustainable,” the letter by FEI Governance Director Francisco Lima stated.The crisis follows the Delhi high court’s dissolution of the EFI executive committee in Feb 2026. Its elected tenure had expired in Sept 2023, while fresh elections remain pending nine months after the court’s intervention. The Indian Olympic Association (IOA) constituted an ad hoc committee on March 27 to oversee the federation and facilitate the electoral process.While acknowledging the committee’s Sept 27 submission and its work, the FEI said elections were expected by Jan 31, 2027. However, the suspension will be reviewed only after the polls are held and evaluated by the international body.The consequences are sweeping. Citing its statutes, the FEI said the EFI “may not attend or be represented at any session or meeting of any FEI body, nor may it organise international events.” More damagingly, athletes, officials, trainers and horses “may not participate in international events organised by the FEI or any other national federation, whether under the Indian flag or the FEI flag.”With the suspension taking effect before the stated election deadline, Indian riders risk losing crucial international competition opportunities. Their return will depend on the completion of elections and the FEI’s subsequent evaluation, leaving athletes caught in a governance crisis they did not create.
Article Summary: The International Equestrian Federation (FEI) has decided to suspend the EFI from Dec 1 over prolonged governance irregularities and failure to hold fresh elections. Indian riders now face a ban from international competitions, with their sporting futures hanging in the balance. The latest setback comes at a time when the govt is pushing to bring more international events to India and widen Indian athletes' exposure to global competition.

Former Australia captain Steve Smith has been cleared of concussion and resumed fielding duties on the fifth day of the first Test against South Africa at Kingsmead in Durban on Tuesday, after undergoing a series of clinical assessments following a blow to the helmet.The 37-year-old batter was struck by a short-pitched delivery from Anrich Nortje during Australia's second innings. Smith attempted to duck under the ball but misjudged its trajectory as it failed to rise as much as he expected.Although he continued batting after the incident, scoring 27 off 41 balls before being caught at long-on off Simon Harmer, Smith did not take the field when South Africa began their second innings on Monday. Michael Neser served as his substitute fielder during that session.However, Smith returned to the field on Tuesday morning after being cleared under Cricket Australia's concussion protocols. He was stationed in the slip cordon when South Africa resumed their chase and subsequently took a catch to dismiss Kyle Verreynne off Matt Renshaw's bowling."Steve Smith has undergone a series of clinical assessments over the past 24 hours in accordance with Cricket Australia’s concussion protocols and has been cleared to take the field this morning," Cricket Australia said in a statement.The incident brought back memories of Smith's previous concussion scare during the 2019 Ashes in England, when he was struck on the head by fast bowler Jofra Archer and forced to miss part of a Test match.Smith's return to the field came after medical assessments over the preceding 24 hours, with Australia following the prescribed protocols before allowing the experienced batter to resume his duties.His presence was a boost for Australia as they pushed for victory in the series opener, with South Africa mounting a determined resistance on the final day.South Africa resumed at 102/4 on Tuesday, needing another 319 runs to win. They reached 166/6 by lunch after Australia struck twice to strengthen their grip on the contest.Opener Aiden Markram led the home side's resistance, remaining unbeaten on 69 at the interval alongside Marco Jansen on seven. The pair had to rebuild after Wiaan Mulder's patient 69-run fifth-wicket partnership with Markram ended when Josh Hazlewood had Mulder caught behind by Alex Carey.Part-time spinner Matt Renshaw then dismissed Verreynne, who made just one before edging a reckless shot to Smith at slip.Renshaw has been Australia's standout performer with the bat, having scored 190 in the first innings and 82 in the second, before adding two wickets to his match contribution.Australia needed four more wickets at lunch to seal victory in the opening Test. The second Test of the series is scheduled to begin in Gqeberha on Sunday.

Naman Dhir had been waiting for a proper opportunity with the bat during his West Indies white-ball tour of India. While he impressed with his tidy off-spin on batting-friendly surfaces, meaningful time in the middle was hard to come by. His breakthrough came in the final T20I in Bengaluru last Saturday, when he smashed an unbeaten 24 off just six balls before rain brought an early end to the match. Five days later, on the other side of the globe, Dhir further strengthened his credentials, guiding India to victory with an unbeaten 42 off 15 balls against New Zealand in Christchurch.Ever since the 2019 ODI World Cup, India have been searching for a middle-order batter capable of contributing valuable overs with the ball. The team's dependence on Hardik Pandya as a seam-bowling all-rounder and the gradual decline of Ravindra Jadeja's role left a noticeable gap, particularly in SENA conditions. Axar Patel and Washington Sundar were both tried, but neither managed to make the role their own over an extended period.At the start of 2026, Riyan Parag, before his hamstring injury, and Ayush Badoni appeared ahead in the pecking order. In the space of a month, however, Dhir has surged to the front of the queue. Seen as Ajit Agarkar 's final major selection punt before stepping down as chairman of selectors, the Mumbai batter is quietly making a strong case for himself."He gives us a lot of options, especially against left-handers with his off-spin, and even against right-handers on certain surfaces. Those two or three crucial overs can change the momentum of a game," India T20I captain Shreyas Iyer said after Thursday's opening T20I. Article Title: Sanju Samson's blazing 67 sets up India's record T20I chase against New Zealand
Article Text:
Sanju Samson and Abhishek Sharma

There were concerns around the Indian team being jetlagged when it arrived at Christchurch’s Hagley Oval for the first T20I against New Zealand on Thursday. After all, the team were involved in a T20I series-decider vs West Indies in Bengaluru last Saturday.By the end of the Powerplay in India’s innings, however, it was the hosts who looked dazed as Sanju Samson and Abhishek Sharma unleashed another of their trademark assaults in pursuit of 226. Samson’s dazzling 67 off 33 balls laid the foundation for India’s highest successful T20I chase, with Naman Dhir’s unbeaten 42 off 15 balls sealing a four-wicket victory with two deliveries to spare.There is a striking simplicity to the way Samson and Abhishek go about their business. Compulsively, they seem to challenge the 100-run mark in the Powerplay. Scoring at least 80-plus, now seems routine. On Thursday, it was Samson who led the charge as India raced to 94/1 in six overs, with Abhishek contributing a brisk 29 off 12 before falling off the penultimate ball of the Powerplay. The significance and impact of Samson’s knock extended beyond just the runs. It bought valuable time for captain Shreyas Iyer to assess the large boundaries and rebuild after India stumbled against Mitchell Santner and Michael Bracewell.From 93 without loss, India slipped to 122/4, briefly allowing New Zealand to get back into the contest. The hosts hardly helped themselves. Adam Milne and Lockie Ferguson struggled for control, conceding 16 wides, while New Zealand also shelled three catches. By then, Samson and Abhishek had already shaken the home side’s confidence. Every one of Samson’s eight fours and four sixes seemed to drive a dagger in their hearts and hopes. India’s T20 blueprint is now well established. Their openers are encouraged to attack relentlessly, irrespective of the target. “Even if we are chasing 170 and we’ve got off to a flyer, we make sure we kill the game in the Powerplay itself. That’s what we’ve been doing really well in the last couple of years,” Samson said after the match.The high-risk and high-reward approach has the potential to backfire too but Samson stressed about the importance of self-belief and the attitude of keeping the team first at all times. The aggression is tactical rather than reckless. Samson’s greatest strength is his ability to remain composed amid the chaos. He rarely appears rushed, even while dismantling bowling attacks. Against New Zealand, he dealt comfortably with the short-ball ploy before unfurling a series of clean straight hits that left the bowlers searching for answers. Standing slightly leg-side of the ball, he created room to access different parts of the ground without sacrificing shape or balance.Brief scores: New Zealand 225/4 in 20 overs (Finn Allen 45, Glenn Phillips 82 n.o.; Mayank Yadav 1-40) lost to India 230/6 in 19.4 overs (Sanju Samson 67, Shreyas Iyer 42, Naman Dhir 42 n.o; Michael Bracewell 2-37).
Article Summary: India beat New Zealand by four wickets in the first T20I in Christchurch. Sanju Samson and Abhishek Sharma scored 67 runs each in India's chase of 226. Naman Dhir’s unbeaten 42 off 15 balls sealed a four-wicket victory.

Article Title: Harry Brook breaks Shubman Gill's fastest 200 record as Sri Lanka pull off historic ODI run chase

England captain Harry Brook made history by scoring the fastest double-century in One-Day International (ODI) cricket, but his record-breaking innings could not prevent Sri Lanka from securing a thrilling two-wicket victory in their tri-series match on Thursday. Sri Lanka chased down a target of 430 with one ball remaining, leaving England at the bottom of the standings after two defeats.Brook reached his double-century in just 114 balls, breaking the previous record of 117 deliveries held by India's Shubman Gill. The 27-year-old also became the first English batter to score an ODI double-century, surpassing Ben Stokes' previous national record of 182 runs.He smashed 202 runs off 116 balls, hitting 21 fours and 10 sixes before being caught by Sahan Arachchige off Janith Liyanage on the final ball of England's innings. Joe Root also contributed with 69 runs off 66 balls as England posted a massive 429-4.Brook, however, was disappointed that his historic achievement ended in defeat."Unfortunately, it (the record) doesn't matter now. I thought we were going to be in a good position but, unfortunately, it doesn't even count," Brook said."Heart-breaking. I think you've hit the nail on the head there. It's very disappointing that we haven't been able to defend 430, but that's life, that's cricket," he added.Sri Lanka produced a remarkable batting display to complete the second-highest successful run chase in ODI history. Pavan Rathnayake led the charge with 130 off 106 balls, while Avishka Fernando and Dasun Shanaka both missed their centuries by just three runs.Sri Lanka needed six runs from the final two balls when Liyanage hit Josh Tongue for a six over long-off to seal victory with one delivery remaining. Tongue finished as England's leading wicket-taker with 3-79.Brook praised Sri Lanka's performance and admitted England failed to execute their bowling plans."You don't see many teams chase down 430 and hats off to Sri Lanka. They've played exceptionally well. We couldn't execute our skills enough with the ball and, again, they've just played an absolute blinder there ..."England, who lost to Pakistan by 87 runs on Tuesday, now need to win their remaining two matches to keep their hopes of reaching the final in Lahore alive."We'll have a good chat about it now and over the next couple of days. We've got a good opportunity in the next couple of games to really try and get to that final in Lahore."
Article Summary: Sri Lanka beat England by two wickets in their tri-series match on Thursday. Sri Lanka chased down a target of 430 with one ball remaining. Pavan Rathnayake led the charge with 130 off 106 balls, while Avishka Fernando and Dasun Shanaka both missed their centuries by just three runs.

Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Kashif Minhas has captured thousands of photographs of cricketers over the years. He is also an avid birdwatcher who sometimes waits for hours to get that perfect shot. But when his sons are playing and he is busy behind the lens on the ground, the avid shutterbug finds it difficult to keep his nerves in check."I have thousands of photographs of international cricketers. When I am completely focused on a match, I become very attentive to every ball. Capturing a catch at the right moment is special. However, these days, when my sons are playing, I sometimes enjoy watching the cricket live more than photographing it," Kashif Minhas, who runs a car business in Multan for a living, tells TimesofIndia.com.Earlier this year, Kashif was caught on camera by the broadcasters after his elder son, Arafat Minhas, playing only his third ODI, got out against Australia at the Gaddafi Stadium in Lahore. As Arafat was dismissed, Kashif, standing behind the boundary rope with his camera, could not hold back his emotions."I was clicking his photographs, and the moment he got out, I put my hand on the camera and lowered my head. The television cameras caught that reaction, and it went viral," he says."They [the broadcasters] know I am his father, so they often keep a camera on me. I even asked the director not to focus on me because I did not want to be shown in front of everyone. People think I am an official photographer of the Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB), which I am not. I freelance for a local newspaper, Daily Pakistan. But they told me that the visual had helped them garner a lot of views, so I thought, 'Chalo, kisi ka toh bhala ho raha' (At least someone is benefiting from it)," he adds.Kashif, however, was deeply hurt by the false stories that circulated after the visuals went viral."That story made me sad. We have been in the car business since 1980, and I have a large showroom in Multan. Some people portrayed the story as if we belonged to a poor family and I had started photographing my children because we had run out of money. That is not the case. Photography is just my hobby. I have a very good car business and import cars from Japan. I never needed money to fund my children's cricket," he says.Kashif's two sons, Arafat Minhas and Sameer Minhas, have shown the world what they are capable of. Arafat has played five ODIs and seven T20Is for Pakistan. The all-rounder has already taken two five-wicket hauls, one each against Australia and England, in his brief international career. Sameer Minhas has lit up age-group cricket, and one cannot forget his 172 off 113 balls against India in the 2025 U-19 Asia Cup final.Kashif says his third son is also getting ready."The world doesn't know about my third son, Abdullah Minhas. He is immensely talented as well. He is a left-handed top-order batter and a right-arm leg-break bowler. He has been selected at the Under-17 level and is working hard," says a proud father.Like many fathers in the subcontinent, Kashif, too, is a cricket tragic."I was also a cricketer. I represented my regional team in Multan. But my father asked me to quit cricket and focus on the family business. He told me to leave cricket or leave home. I left home for two or three days, but then my mother asked me to come back and give up cricket. Nothing is more important to me than my mother, so I quit," he recalls.But one fine day, while playing with a tape ball in their car porch, Kashif's eyes lit up when he saw Arafat and Sameer, then aged nine and seven, respectively, cutting, driving and pulling."The floor was wet, and their hand-eye coordination was amazing. When I saw my children playing, I immediately realised that they had something special in them. I decided that what had happened to me should not happen to them. I wanted them to have the opportunity to pursue cricket," he says."I took them to a local cricket academy, and when I saw how well they were playing against pace, I began to take their cricket more seriously. Arafat performed well in the PCB Under-13 tournament, then at the Under-16 and Under-19 levels. Sameer followed in his footsteps, and soon Abdullah will do the same. We kept trying and praying, and Allah blessed us," he adds.Kashif, who had to give up his own cricketing ambitions, acknowledges that cricket is a tough sport to succeed in and requires much more than time and money."It requires a lot of dedication. You have to make sacrifices. I was away with my children for their training when I heard the news of my father's death. After his demise, I had to spend a lot of time at the office. But whenever they played matches outside Multan, I would travel and sit at the ground from morning until evening," he recalls.As his sons progressed through age-group cricket, Kashif came up with the idea of taking up photography as a way to stay close to them. He started freelancing and soon found work with a local daily. As Arafat and Sameer began making waves with their performances, Kashif, too, became a familiar face on cricket grounds across Pakistan, camera in hand."It was an amazing moment for me," says Kashif, recalling Arafat's ODI debut against Australia in Rawalpindi."I never imagined that a day would come when my children would represent Pakistan in international cricket and I would be on the ground photographing them. It felt like a blessing, and I was very happy that day. He [Arafat] performed well in the last match [against England]," he further adds.Kashif has never been harsh on his sons regarding cricket. But he has one dream he hopes to fulfil through them: winning an ICC trophy."I was never harsh on them. When they were not performing well, I would tell them that it was not their day and that their time would come. I would encourage them to stay prepared for the next opportunity. I never wanted to put unnecessary pressure on them. But I will be even happier when my children win an ICC trophy for their country," he says.The Minhas family could have etched its name in the Guinness World Records, with members representing Pakistan at different age-group levels. But the PCB has declined a request from the over-50s team to participate in the International Masters Cricket World Cup, which is being hosted by India in January next year.Minhas Sr was a member of that squad. Pakistan won the previous edition of the tournament, held in Sri Lanka last year, but this time the board has informed the Pakistan Veterans Cricket Association that its team will not be permitted to travel to India and participate."It would have been great to represent Pakistan, but it's okay. I will get the chance later," he says.For Kashif Minhas, cricket has come full circle. He once had to abandon his own ambitions at his father's insistence, but he made sure his sons had the freedom to pursue theirs. Today, he watches them represent Pakistan, capturing their highs and lows through his lens while carrying the hopes of a father who knows what it means to let go of a dream. An ICC trophy would be the ultimate reward, but for Kashif, seeing his sons live the dream he once had to give up is already a journey worth cherishing.
Article Summary: Kashif Minhas has captured thousands of photographs of cricketers over the years. He is also an avid birdwatcher who sometimes waits for hours to get that perfect shot. Kashif's two sons, Arafat Minhas and Sameer Minhas, have shown the world what they are capable of.

Abhishek Sharma set a new record for hitting the first ball he faced for a six most often in T20Is, but India had a huge target to chase after New Zealand posted 225/8 in the opening T20I in Christchurch on Thursday.Chasing 226, Abhishek faced his first delivery off the final ball of the first over and sent Matt Henry over the cover boundary for a six. Henry bowled a full delivery wide of off stump, but Abhishek went through with his lofted drive and cleared the ropes to reach the milestone.Abhishek has now hit the first ball he faced for a six seven times in T20Is, moving ahead of Afghanistan's Shafiqullah Shinwari, who has done so six times. Suryakumar Yadav is third on the list with five such sixes, while Ireland's Paul Stirling, New Zealand's Colin Munro and the UAE's Mohammad Naveed have managed it four times each.Abhishek and Sanju Samson gave India the quick start they needed, putting together 93 runs for the opening wicket in just 5.5 overs. However, Michael Bracewell ended the partnership by dismissing Abhishek for 29 off 12 balls.The left-hander struck three sixes and two fours during his brief innings.The partnership also saw Abhishek and Samson equal the record for the most 50-plus opening stands by an Indian pair in T20Is in a calendar year. Their stand was their fifth such partnership in 2026, putting them alongside two other Indian pairs on the list.Earlier, Finn Allen and Glenn Phillips led New Zealand to 225/8, the joint-highest total against India in T20Is and New Zealand's highest on home soil. Allen scored 45 off 24 balls, while Phillips remained unbeaten on 82 off 40 deliveries.With Jasprit Bumrah not part of the squad, India's bowlers struggled to contain the hosts. Despite some early swing, New Zealand's batters found ways to score freely, adding 67 runs in the final five overs.Axar Patel was India's most expensive bowler, conceding 51 runs in four overs. The innings also brought an unwanted record for India, as five bowlers conceded 40 or more runs in a T20I innings for the first time. It was the 13th such instance in men's T20Is overall.Bhuvneshwar Kumar conceded 49 runs in his four overs, Arshdeep Singh gave away 45, Mayank Yadav and Nitish Reddy conceded 40 each, while Axar finished with figures of 1/51.At the time of writing the story, India were 128/4 in 11 overs.
Article Summary: Abhishek Sharma sets new record for most sixes off first ball faced in T20Is. India chase 226 after New Zealand post 225/8 in opening T20I in Christchurch. Five bowlers conceded 40 or more runs in a T20i innings for the first time.

Athletes compete from a throwing chair and use their arms and upper-body strength to throw the discus.Limited trunk control can affect how they balance and generate power during a throw.
Article Summary: Suvarna Raj, 44, won gold for India in the women's F54 discus throw at the Asian Para Games on Thursday. She finished first with a best throw of 15.66m, adding another medal to her international career. Suvarna is also an accessibility specialist and disability rights advocate. She has carried out more than 1,000 accessibility audits across India.

Article Title: Sexual offence charge rocks India's Asian Para Games contingent; swimmer faces lifetime ban
Article Text:
Mohammad Shams Aalam Shaikh (Image credit: Instagram)

NEW DELHI: The Indian contingent at the Asian Para Games in Nagoya has been left embarrassed after para swimmer Mohammad Shams Aalam Shaikh was detained by Japanese police following allegations of sexually harassing and molesting a female hotel employee. The 40-year-old, once a world No 1 in his event, was sent back to India on Tuesday, a day after the alleged incident, and faces the prospect of a lifetime ban from the Paralympic Committee of India (PCI).A senior PCI official, who is part of the Indian delegation in Nagoya and who handled the entire situation, confirmed the development to TOI, describing the alleged misconduct as “reprehensible and intolerable” and saying there could be “no justification” for such behaviour by an athlete representing the country on the international stage.”“Aalam is staring at no less than a lifetime ban for bringing disrepute to the entire Indian delegation participating at the Asian Para Games and for embarrassing the country on the world stage,” the official said.According to the official, the incident occurred on Monday at the Four Points by Sheraton hotel, where the Indian para swimming team was staying. The female employee was reportedly carrying out housekeeping duties in the swimmer’s room when the alleged misconduct took place.“The local organising committee (LOC) informed the chef-de-mission’s (CDM) office that an alleged sexual harassment and molestation incident had occurred at the hotel and that an Indian athlete had been detained by the local police,” the official said.“When we reached the hotel, the police and senior hotel managers were already there. We were told that the athlete had inappropriately touched the female housekeeping staff member, made sexually coloured gestures, attempted to grope her and made sexual advances. She rushed out and informed her superiors. This is what we were told by the police and hotel staff,” the official added.The official said the delegation apologised to the hotel authorities and the employee. Following the complaint, police detained Shaikh and took him to a local police station. The official said the authorities sought his arrest and that he be formally presented before a court.The LOC subsequently intervened, with the Indian delegation asked to furnish a written apology to the employee and ensure that the athlete left Japan. Shaikh was moved to another hotel for the night and booked on the first available flight, departing Nagoya at around 2 pm local time on Tuesday, the official said. He was released after the written apology was furnished, according to the official’s account.“The police authorities had clearly recorded the sexual offence allegation in their formal complaint, in Japanese. We can confirm that since I saw that,” the official said.The official added the incident had diverted senior Indian officials from the contingent’s ongoing sporting campaign. “Instead of focusing on the Games and our athletes’ performances, we spent several hours at the police station and later at the hotel premises convincing the authorities. We were embarrassed in front of everyone,” the official said.He added that the employee appeared to be in deep shock when the delegation returned to the hotel. The hotel and LOC, he said, sought updates on the action India would take and warned that they could pursue formal legal proceedings if they were dissatisfied with the response.The PCI has informed the govt in New Delhi of the proposed action, the official said. After the Games, PCI officials, para swimming administrators and members of the delegation will deliberate on the matter and recommend stringent sanctions to the sports ministry and Sports Authority of India (SAI).“The CDM’s office has already recommended a lifetime ban. A formal decision will be taken at a meeting in Delhi after we return,” the official said.Shaikh, who hails from Bihar’s Madhubani district and lives with his family in Mumbai’s Dharavi, was sent home without competing in his scheduled events on Wednesday.A former world No. 1 in the men’s 100m butterfly (S5) and 50m breaststroke (SB4), according to World Para Swimming records, Shaikh represented India at the 2018 Asian Para Games in Jakarta and won 200m breaststroke gold at the Reykjavik International Games last year, setting Indian and Asian records.The incident comes close on the heels of an Indian hockey umpire and technical official Gurinder Singh Sangha was being sent home from the able-bodied Asian Games in Nagoya following sexual misconduct and harassment complaints by a Malaysian hockey official and a hotel staff member.
Article Summary: Para swimmer Mohammad Shams Aalam Shaikh was detained by Japanese police following allegations of sexually harassing and molesting a female hotel employee. The 40-year-old, once a world No 1 in his event, was sent back to India on Tuesday, a day after the alleged incident. Shaikh faces the prospect of a lifetime ban from the Paralympic Committee of India.

Article Title: Decoding the business of bringing Brazil, Uruguay, Panama to India for football friendlies
Article Text:
Soccer Football - International Friendly - India v Brazil - Salt Lake Stadium, Kolkata, India - October 3, 2026 Brazil's Vinicius Junior in action with India's Ryan Williams REUTERS/Sahiba Chawdhary

New Delhi:

Who pays for the spectacle?

Supporters cheer for their teams during the International Friendly football match between India and Brazil at Vivekananda Yuba Bharati Krirangan, in Kolkata. (ANI)

Brazilian player Pedro (19) celebrates after his goal during an international friendly football match between India and Brazil at the Vivekananda Yuba Bharati Krirangan (Salt Lake Stadium) in Kolkata. (PTI)

The problem with selling a Brazil match

India and Brazil football players during the international friendly match at the Vivekananda Yuba Bharati Krirangan (Salt Lake Stadium) in Kolkata. (PTI)

A delegation of the Brazilian Football Confederation and others inspect the field at Salt lake Stadium, also known as Vivekananda Yuba Bharati Krirangan (PTI Photo/Swapan Mahapatra)

Why planning matters more than ticket prices

Brazil supporters during the FIFA friendly between India and Brazil at the Salt Lake Stadium in Kolkata. (Image: PTI)

Kohana, her husband and four boys travelled from Chennai to Kolkata for the India vs Brazil game. (Image: Tanuj Lakhina/TimesofIndia.com)

Angry fans vandalised the Salt Lake Stadium, alleging poor management during Argentine footballer Lionel Messi's G.O.A.T India Tour 2025 in Kolkata. (ANI)

Why government backing matters

I think there's a lot of negative news around (Indian) football. So as long as that's there, the appetite will be limited. But I think this one event will change the appetite for future events. Anuj Kichlu

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Bringing Brazil to India was not just about getting one of football's biggest names to play a match. It was about negotiating with federations, securing the right venue, arranging travel and accommodation, ensuring security, maintaining the pitch and, ultimately, figuring out who will pay for it all.The financial stakes are substantial. An international friendly involving a World Cup nation can cost at least Rs 10 crore, while staging a match involving one of the biggest teams could push the bill to Rs 100 crore, according to Anuj Kichlu, director and CEO of Best of You, which helped facilitate India's friendlies against Panama, Brazil and Uruguay "It would happen depending on the team. But an international friendly of a World Cup nation kind of friendly will not come under 10 crores," Kichlu told TimesofIndia.com after the three friendlies in Bengaluru and Kolkata."I'm saying you take the cost of the team, the cost of their travel, the cost of the stadium, event, and that. So the lowest you'll get a World Cup team is at Rs 10 crores, and the highest it'll cost is even 100 crores for one match, depending on the team."The figures, he explained, cover considerably more than the fee for securing a team's appearance."It's appearance, logistics, flights, hotels, securities, player's safety, police, in-stadium branding, event management, insurances.Everything would be covered," he explained.The challenge, therefore, is not simply to bring a marquee team to India. It is to make the economics of the event work in a market where the appetite for international football is still developing.There is no single business model for staging an international friendly. The financial structure depends on who initiates the event and what they hope to achieve.A private promoter may organise a match with the expectation of recovering the investment through ticket sales, sponsorships and broadcast rights. A football federation, meanwhile, may be driven by sporting objectives, including giving its national team exposure against stronger opposition.In the case of India's recent friendlies, the AIFF approached the Spain-headquartered Best of You to help bring international teams to the country. They acted as a match agent, negotiating with the visiting federations and coordinating arrangements for their participation. Commercialisation, including ticketing and broadcasting, was handled separately by the AIFF and its agencies.Kichlu was clear about the distinction."Yeah, they engaged agencies for sponsorship. They engaged agencies for ticketing. They had security agencies for private security. They engaged with several different vendors, 5-6 different vendors for different roles," said Kichlu, who leads the company's India office.They, meanwhile, are not necessarily the party carrying the event's commercial risk."It's two federations only, and we come in as match agents. So we are not actually a party on the contract, but we are match agents on the contract," he said on how the agreement is drawn.He explained that the agent's responsibilities included areas such as insurance and cancellation, rather than the commercialisation of the event.That separation is important. While the agent helps secure the teams and ensure contractual obligations are met, the federation and its commercial partners must work out whether the event can generate enough revenue to justify the expenditure.Brazil was the centrepiece of the three friendly series, for which India opted against playing the FIFA ASEAN Cup , selected for its substantial fan following in India, especially in Kolkata. Panama was brought in as a preparatory opponent, while Uruguay was added later when an opportunity arose to secure the team at a comparatively favourable price during their tour of Japan and South Korea.But the appeal of a famous team does not automatically translate into a commercially successful event.Kichlu believes the market for international football in India has potential, although negative publicity surrounding the sport has affected confidence among both spectators and sponsors."I think there's a lot of negative news around (Indian) football. So as long as that's there, the appetite will be limited. But I think this one event will change the appetite for future events."He said the matches had generated interest in future fixtures, despite the commercial challenges."So already we are getting inquiries for future matches and stuff in India because this one was successful, other than commercially. If you see everything on the ground was quite successful."For sponsors, however, interest alone is insufficient. Brands want measurable evidence that an event can deliver an audience and provide value for their investment."Not only fans, even I'd say sponsors obviously are reluctant to associate with something if they don't have numbers and backing, right? So when you go to someone and say you're sponsoring a Brazil match and they ask you for data of another big match in India, you don't have a match to go by," he stated.The lack of comparable events makes it difficult to establish what sponsors should expect from a major international friendly. Television ratings, digital views and stadium attendance can offer useful indicators, but they need to be interpreted carefully.Kichlu pointed out that even television figures can be difficult to assess without knowing how long viewers watched. Digital views, too, do not necessarily reflect sustained engagement. The recent elation with viewership of the Indian Super League (ISL) is an example of keeping caution.The friendlies, meanwhile, could therefore serve as a reference point for future commercial decisions."So decisions in the future will be made based on these 3 matches and the UK tour (Unity Cup against Nigeria and Zimbabwe) and stuff like that," said Kichlu.For Indian football, the ability to turn those experiences into reliable audience data could be as important as securing the next marquee opponent.The attendance at the Salt Lake Stadium for the friendlies against Brazil and Uruguay raised eyebrows. 51,402 came through the gates for the Brazil game and 37,307 for the contest against Uruguay. Different reasons have been suggested for the less-than-expected turnout. Kichlu believes the marketing window and the timing of the event played a significant role."I think the marketing for the match was pretty late, to be honest, because with the kind of prices they're charging for those tickets, it means it's not that people aren't willing to pay it," he said."I think it just needs more planning because people will dedicate budgets to this compared to something else, and I would say a lot of people would have committed money somewhere else," he continued.The short lead time also limited the opportunity to attract fans from outside Kolkata."And with a 2-3 week window only, people would have made other plans to travel to other places. Being a long weekend also, I would say a lot of the people from Bombay, Delhi, Bangalore, stuff like that, would have made other plans to go on holidays in other places."His argument is that a match involving Brazil should not be marketed only to the city hosting it. It has the potential to draw spectators from across India, but doing so requires advance planning."But if they had, say, a 2-and-a-half, 3-month notice, they would have probably planned towards this.""I think the disappointing thing was that the number of people from across India who traveled for the match was low compared to what you would expect for this kind of a match."Concerns about safety following the earlier Lionel Messi event in Kolkata had, he said, made some parents cautious about bringing their children to another high-profile football event."I think we have to work more on the family experience and obviously giving more time and with that, it'll work."He does not believe ticket prices and it coming two weeks before Durga Puja explain the lower attendance."To be honest, the pricing of the tickets, I've researched all over Asia and even countries who are as far as India, and people are willing to pay this and much more for these kind of matches.""So I don't think it's that much of the ticketing price. I think it's the people who are willing to pay for these tickets are the ones who didn't come to the stadium," he reasoned.If ticketing and sponsorship alone cannot guarantee a return, who should pay for the difference?Kichlu believes government support can be crucial when a country is trying to establish itself as a destination for major international football."I think government should play more of a role, right? If they want to bring these events, like, any state government wants to bring these kind of events to their state, they'd have to also pitch in resources. That's exactly why Brazil went to Australia.""The two matches were funded by the Queensland state government. It was part of their objective to promote the state internationally."The investment, in such cases, is not necessarily intended to be recovered entirely through ticket sales. Governments may see international sporting events as a way to promote a destination, generate publicity and build the infrastructure and reputation required to host larger events.Kichlu said the economics in established football markets are different for such friendlies because ticketing and broadcast revenues are more predictable."In Europe, you can take a team and you can make it commercially viable because the market is there, people are willing to pay it."In emerging markets, he argued, the commercial foundations are not yet as secure."And if you don't do that, I don't think these events are economical to organise like it is in Europe, where you have a set ticket price you can charge. You know what broadcast rights you'll get. You know what sponsorship you'll get. Everything is starting at a base level. So you have to have backing," he finished.
Article Summary: An international friendly involving a World Cup nation can cost at least Rs 10 crore. Staging a match involving one of the biggest teams could push the bill to Rs 100 crore. Financial structure depends on who initiates the event and what they hope to achieve.

What the names say about Messi’s legacy

Argentina's Lionel Messi celebrates after scoring his side���s third goal from the penalty spot during his final match for the national team, a soccer friendly against Benin, in Buenos Aires, Argentina, Tuesday, Oct.6, 2026. AP/PTI(AP10_08_2026_000008B)

Messi is not the first footballer honoured by science

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Neotrichia pelei

A sage plant discovered in the Peruvian Andes has become the sixth species named after Lionel Messi , extending a record already shared by a lizard, spider, fossil brachiopod, condor and fungus. The newly describedcarries Argentina’s familiar blue and white colours in its flowers, but the tribute comes with a troubling detail: researchers have classified the plant as endangered.is a sage species endemic to the Andes of central and southern Peru, where it grows on rocky, arid slopes between 2,000 and 2,400 metres above sea level. It belongs to the mint family, Lamiaceae, which includes plants associated with antioxidant, anti-inflammatory and antiseptic properties.The plant can grow to approximately 1.5 metres tall, with pale blue and white flowers that resemble Argentina’s national colours. Those colours make the choice of namesake especially fitting for a footballer who represented his country across a career spanning more than two decades.The name follows botanical naming conventions, which often adapt a person’s surname into Latin. The ending “i” indicates possession, socan be understood as “Messi’s sage”.The species was described by researchers led by Paul Gonzales of the Natural History Museum at the National University of San Marcos, alongside Argentine researcher Rolando Uria and biologist Jean Capcha-Ramos of Huarango Nature. Their study appeared in the October edition of the botanical journalThe plant’s restricted range and endangered classification give the discovery significance beyond its unusual celebrity namesake. Its name may draw attention to the species, but its survival depends on protecting the mountain habitat where it grows.In May 2024, Guinness World Records recognised Messi as the footballer with the most species named after him, recording five at the time.now brings that total to six.The names span living animals, prehistoric fossils, fungi and now a flowering plant. The fossil condor and brachiopod also show that the honour is not limited to species alive today.Messi’s record is unusual, although he is not the only footballer whose name has entered scientific classification. Diego Maradona has been associated with four named organisms, but one, the fairy wasp, was later found to be the same species as an earlier-named wasp and is therefore no longer considered valid.Messi’s name has reached science through a series of researchers choosing to recognise his influence, rather than through any single award or official campaign. The latest example connects his sporting identity directly with Argentina’s colours, even though the plant itself grows across the border in Peru.The tribute also arrives after a remarkable international career. Messi made his senior Argentina debut against Hungary on 17 August 2005, briefly retired from international football in 2016, then returned to lead the team through its major successes.He captained Argentina to Copa América titles in 2021 and 2024 and the 2022 World Cup triumph in Qatar. Messi has made 208 appearances and scored 126 goals for Argentina, winning the Ballon d’Or eight times. He scored in Argentina’s 3-0 victory over Benin in his final international match earlier this month. Now 39, he continues his club career with Inter Miami and has also been nominated among the 30 contenders for the 2026 Ballon d’Or.The practice of naming newly described organisms after footballers goes back further than Messi’s record. In December 2009, researchers named 12 newly described microcaddisfly species after members of Brazil’s 1958 World Cup-winning team, including Pelé, whose name was given toMaradona’s scientific namesakes include a fossil damselfly, a parasitic fluke and a sea snail, alongside the wasp later found not to be a distinct species.For Messi, the new sage adds another entry to a record already recognised by Guinness, while also drawing attention to a plant whose future is less secure than the footballer’s place in the sport’s history. The sixth namesake may be a small botanical discovery, but it carries both a tribute and a reminder of the biodiversity researchers are still identifying.
Article Summary: Messi’s latest botanical honour takes his Guinness World Records tally to six species, including animals, fossils and fungi. A sage plant discovered in the Peruvian Andes has become the sixth species named after Lionel Messi, extending a record already shared by a lizard, spider, fossil brachiopod, condor and fungus.

Article Title: Why Portugal fined Cristiano Ronaldo exactly €255 for walking out despite his massive $1.2 billion net worth: Reason beind modest penalty
Article Text:
Cristiano Ronaldo received exactly €255 fine and a backdated suspension, raising questions over how Portugal determined the penalty for walking out.

Ronaldo was fined under a rule covering players who abandon national duty

The €255 figure comes from a fixed accounting unit
